extra.message: The 'name' query parameter is concatenated directly into a filesystem path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) and the raw request body is written to it. A value like '../../../../etc/cron.d/x' or an absolute path traverses outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR, allowing arbitrary file write/overwrite on the server filesystem.

User-controlled 'expr' GET parameter is passed directly to eval(). Although __builtins__ is stripped, Python object introspection (e.g. via attribute chains on the provided ints) can still be used to escape the sandbox and execute arbitrary code. This is a classic unsafe eval() code-injection pattern.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code (Eval Injection)

extra.message: User-controlled 'fragment' GET parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered directly. This is Server-Side Template Injection: an attacker can supply Jinja2 expressions/statements (e.g. via {{ }} or {% %} blocks) that execute arbitrary Python and achieve remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine (SSTI)

extra.message: The 'filter' field of the parsed JSON request body is passed unmodified as the MongoDB query document to find_one(). An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators (e.g. {"$where": ...} or $regex) to bypass intended filtering or cause a NoSQL injection / denial of service.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: appointment_cancel() only verifies ownership for patient users (appt.patient != request.user.patient_profile). Unlike the sibling appointment_edit/appointment_complete views, it never checks that a clinician's appt.provider matches request.user.provider_profile. Any authenticated clinician can POST to /appointments/<uuid>/cancel/ for an appointment belonging to a different provider's patient and cancel it, a broken access control / IDOR flaw.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Elevated 'lane' access (payroll/casework data) is granted purely based on a client-supplied cookie or header ('ops_badge'/'x-ops-badge') equalling the hardcoded string 'lead'. Any caller who already knows or guesses this literal value can self-elevate privileges without any real authentication.

The 'copyline' GET parameter is concatenated directly into an HTML response body (text/html) with no escaping, allowing reflected Cross-Site Scripting via a payload such as ?copyline=<script>alert(1)</script>.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS)

extra.message: The 'lane' GET/POST parameter is passed unvalidated to redirect(), letting an attacker craft a link to this endpoint that redirects victims to an arbitrary external, attacker-controlled URL (e.g. ?lane=https://evil.example).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: The Origin request header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. This lets any arbitrary origin make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the response, defeating the same-origin policy entirely.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The full raw request body and the Authorization header are written to the application log at WARNING level. Bearer tokens/credentials and any sensitive payload contents end up persisted in plaintext log files.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The endpoint returns a hardcoded live-looking partner API token ('sync_key': 'tok_live_partner_sync') and what appears to be a hardcoded SSN-formatted value ('tax_ref': '739-44-1982') to any caller possessing the internal ops token, exposing a credential and sensitive PII in the API response.

Identity verification relies on a small hardcoded dictionary of static verifier codes ({'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}) compared with a non-constant-time '!=' check. These fixed codes are embedded in source and never rotate, making brute-force or code leakage trivially exploitable.

Unlike every other handler in this module, patient_identity_ping_345() never calls _wrk_gate(request) before processing the request. It is reachable by any unauthenticated caller at /ops/identity/patient-ping-345/, breaking the internal-only access model the rest of the module relies on.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: ssl._create_unverified_context() disables TLS certificate and hostname verification for the outbound request to the partner endpoint, allowing man-in-the-middle interception/tampering of the connection.

When a staff user (which includes the 'clinician' role via is_staff_role) uploads a document, the target patient is taken directly from request.POST['patient_id'] with only get_object_or_404 — there is no check that the patient is assigned to that clinician (unlike document_detail/document_download which check assigned_patients or an existing appointment). A clinician can upload/attach documents to any patient's chart, not just their own patients.

An arbitrary attacker-supplied JSON object (change_set) is merged with dict.update() into a workspace dict that contains privilege-sensitive keys ('role', 'is_admin', 'credit_limit') without any allowlist of permitted fields, a mass-assignment pattern that would be dangerous if this dict were ever persisted or used for an authorization decision.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: A 'code' value is generated using the non-cryptographic random.choice()/random module. If this code is used anywhere as a security token or nonce, it is predictable and unsuitable for security purposes; secrets.choice() should be used instead.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: The response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and an empty Content-Security-Policy header, actively disabling browser XSS mitigations for this endpoint.

The endpoint returns internal implementation details (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE environment value and the server's absolute base export directory path) in the JSON response, aiding reconnaissance for further attacks.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded, publicly-visible default ('django-insecure-local-dev-only-change-in-production') and DEBUG defaults to True when the corresponding environment variables are unset, which would expose detailed stack traces/settings and use a known signing key if deployed without overriding these env vars.
